topic: The Great Depression and New Deal

question.leadin: One theory suggests that this woman and Fred Noonan died in the Mariana Islands while in Japanese custody.
question.text: Name this female aviator who left New Guinea aboard her plane, the Electra, but never arrived at Howland Island, which has spawned many theories about her disappearance.
question.clue: In July 2017 National Geographic sent border collies to a Kiribati island to investigate this person, while the History Channel claimed she was captured by the Japanese.

swap.leadin: On "Black Sunday" during this period, so-called "black blizzards" swept through the plains states.
swap.text: "Okies" migrated west during what period of severe drought and agriculture damage in the 1930s?
swap.clue: This event saw numerous storms referred to as black blizzards.

question.text: This 31 st president was largely blamed for the Great Depression, and disgruntled citizens set up makeshift shantytowns sarcastically nicknamed after him.
question.clue: This man led the Food Administration during World War I, and MacArthur disobeyed his command to not attack the Bonus Army.

swap.text: The Great Depression led to the election of Franklin Roosevelt, whose thrity nightly radio addresses from 1933 to 1934 were given this name due to their intimate and calming nature.
swap.clue: Similar speeches were given while their speaker was Governor of New York.

question.text: During this 1929 event carried out on Capone's orders, perpetrated with Thompson submachine guns, several men disguised themselves as police officers and shot 7 of Bugs Moran's associates.
question.clue: The victims of this event had been tricked into believing that they were waiting for a delivery of stolen whiskey.

swap.leadin: This man participated in a campaign where he avidly destroyed pinball machines with sledgehammers.
swap.text: Name this Italian-American mayor who was dubbed "the Little Flower." He co-sponsored an act with Senator George Norris which banned yellow-dog contracts.
swap.answerHtml: Fiorello La Guardia [or Fiorello Henry La Guardia; or Fiorello Raffaele Enrico La Guardia]
swap.clue: While in Congress, this man worked with George Norris to co-sponsor an act that banned yellow-dog contracts.

question.leadin: Harcourt Morgan served on the board of directors for this agency, the constitutionality of which was upheld in the Ashwander case.
question.text: Name this agency created in 1933 that was intended to construct dams on a namesake body of water.
question.clue: The Muscle Shoals Bill, vetoed by Herbert Hoover, was the initial impetus for this organization.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the founder of the Fifth Party System.
swap.text: One of the major contributors to the New Deal was this member of the Brain Trust, who was the first director of the New York City Planning Commission and later governed Puerto Rico.
swap.clue: In another role, this man was influenced by the ideas of Clarence Perry and Clarence Stein in trying to design three thousand self-sufficient communities while working with John Lansill, those communities being known as Greenbelt Towns.

question.leadin: Including over twenty thousand unemployed veterans, it made its way to Washington under the leadership of Walter Waters.
question.text: Name this group of World War I soldiers seeking early payment of their pensions.
question.clue: Pelham Glassford twice reinstated Walter Waters as the leader of this group, which Gladwin Bland described as "an immense hobo jungle."

swap.leadin: This man pushed for the popularization of radio as secretary of commerce, in which capacity he also vastly expand the department by siphoning off poorly managed duties from other agencies.
swap.text: Name this man whose response to the Great Mississippi Flood helped propel him to the presidency, an engineer who saved millions of Europeans from starvation during World War I.
swap.clue: A baby was among the dead after this president ordered a force led by Walter Waters to leave the Anacostia Flats; that Bonus Army was dispersed by Douglas MacArthur.

question.leadin: Note to Players: A description is acceptable for the first part. Handwriting analysis helped convict Bruno Hauptmann for the kidnapping of this person.
question.text: Name or describe this child whose 1932 kidnapping and murder led to a "Trial of the Century" and the passage of the Federal Kidnapping Act.
question.answerHtml: Charles Augustus Lindbergh Jr. [accept answers describing Charles Lindbergh’s son, accept the Lindbergh baby]

swap.leadin: Name the following events that occurred during the presidency of Herbert Hoover.
swap.text: The laissez-faire approach of this man, Hoover's Secretary of the Treasury, worsened the Great Depression.
swap.clue: Those proceedings occurred after this man financially backed Pittsburgh-based members of Cox's Army.

question.leadin: A group of this many Black students in Rock Hill, South Carolina, pioneered the "Jail, No Bail" strategy after being arrested at a sit-in.
question.text: What number also appears in the most common name of a 1972 anti-discrimination provision in education authored primarily by Patsy Mink?
question.answerHtml: nine [accept Title IX; accept Friendship Nine or Rock Hill Nine]
question.clue: Countee Cullen wrote about a group of this many people that ends "Surely, I said, / Now will the poets sing. / But they have raised no cry. / I wonder why."

swap.leadin: Headed by Harry Hopkins, this entity helped create the Federal Theatre Project, which, headed by Hallie Flanagan, helped artists survive in a time of trouble.
swap.text: Name this organization that became the largest relief program in American history as skilled and unskilled workers were employed with large construction and art projects.
swap.answerHtml: Works Progress Administration [do not prompt on “Federal Works Agency” or “Work Projects Administration,” as Hopkins was no longer in charge]
swap.clue: One branch of this organization was led by Hallie Flanagan, under whose leadership that branch undertook news reenactments called the "Living Newspaper," series, while another branch of this organization was responsible for producing the American Guide Series.

question.leadin: Answer stuff about Robert Penn Warren FTPE.
question.text: The Fugitives collected their work in this 1930 anthology defending traditional Southern agrarianism.
question.clue: This compilation featured a "Statement of Principles" that asked how far a group should surrender its "moral, social and economic autonomy, to the victorious principle of Union?"

swap.text: New York City's chief medical examiner, who had this surname, noted that the government "knows it is not stopping drinking" by poisoning alcohol. A senator with this surname drafted workers' rights legislation with Fiorello LaGuardia.

question.leadin: TIME named the leader of this agency, Hugh S. Johnson, as its 1933 Man of the Year instead of FDR after he implemented industry codes to ensure "fair competition."
question.text: A blue eagle and the motto "We Do Our Part" were used to represent what agency, which was dissolved after the Supreme Court ruled its regulations were unconstitutional in the "sick chicken" case?
question.clue: General Hugh Johnson was made the director of this agency, which was created by an act that set up a group of fair competition codes for industry.

swap.leadin: John Hart Ely's Democracy and Distrust builds on Justice Harlan Stone's opinion in this case by arguing that the Warren Court's activism was not values-based but process-based.
swap.text: Name this Supreme Court case, whose Footnote Four introduced the basis for strict scrutiny by proposing a "narrower scope for operation of the presumption of constitutionality."
swap.clue: This 1938 Supreme Court case, which is more famous for its "footnote four."

question.leadin: Name some details of Great Depression-era photographs.
question.text: A portrait of Allie May Burroughs was taken in by this photographer, who documented rural Alabama through staying with the Burroughs, Fields, and Tingle families. He compiled his photos into the collection Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.
question.clue: This photographer took pictures for the Farm Security Administration, documenting the Great Depression in Southern states, particularly Alabama. He collaborated with James Agee on Let Us Now Praise Famous Men.

swap.text: This woman became the first elected female senator after succeeding her husband Thaddeus. An opponent to this woman campaigned under the sexist slogan "Arkansas Needs Another Man in the Senate!"
swap.clue: This female Senator from Arkansas who served until 1944 when she was replaced by J. William Fulbright.
